turns.prompt_text: I have now pulled all of my tax information for the past few years, I would like to complete my 2024 taxes, and then complete my 2025 taxes after. Completing taxes is something I believe I can do myself by now. How can I achieve this for 2024?
turns.response_html:
Tackling your taxes in chronological order is the perfect approach, as certain numbers and carryovers from your 2024 return will be required to accurately complete your 2025 forms. Since the filing deadline for 2024 has passed, you are filing what the IRS considers a prior-year or late return.

Here is how you can self-file for 2024:

If you are owed a refund, there is generally no penalty for filing a late return—you typically have up to three years from the original deadline to claim it. However, if you owe taxes, late filing and payment penalties may apply.

To make sure we get everything squared away correctly before you start calculating, I have a few quick questions:

  • Did you have any freelance or contract income during 2024, or was your income solely from your W-2?
  • What state or states were you a resident of during 2024?
  • Are you expecting a refund for 2024, or do you anticipate owing a balance?

turns.prompt_text: I lived in San Antonio, Texas, for all of 2024, and I did not participate in any freelance or contract income. It was solely Northrop Grumman. I paid a lot in the pre-emptive taxes, so I would have gotten money back.
turns.response_html:
That is fantastic news for this process for two major reasons. First, Texas does not have a state income tax, meaning you only have to worry about filing a federal return. Second, if you are owed a refund, there are absolutely no late penalties, and you have until April 2028 to claim that money.

Since your situation is a straightforward single W-2, here is exactly how to get this knocked out:

1. Track down your W-2

You will need the official 2024 W-2 from Northrop Grumman. If you don't have a physical copy, you should be able to log into their payroll provider (like ADP or Workday) to download the PDF.

2. Use prior-year software

Because you only need to file a federal return, a service like FreeTaxUSA is highly recommended. It is a legitimate, IRS-approved platform that supports prior-year returns, and filing a federal return through them is typically free. You will just need to select their 2024 software version, create an account, and plug in the numbers from your W-2.

3. Print, sign, and mail

As a self-filer handling a past-year return, you generally cannot click "e-file." The software will generate a completed Form 1040 for you to print.

  • Sign and date the form in ink.
  • Attach a copy of your W-2 (usually Copy B) to the designated spot on the front.
  • Mail it to the IRS. Note: Use your current Ames, Iowa address on the tax form so the IRS knows where to reach you or send a paper check if you opt out of direct deposit. You will mail the packet to the IRS processing center designated for Iowa residents.

Once you drop that in the mail, your 2024 obligation is officially handled. The IRS usually takes a bit longer to process paper returns (often 6 to 8 weeks), so your refund might take a little time to hit your bank account.

Are you ready to move right into tackling your 2025 taxes, or do you want to get 2024 printed and mailed first?
